5cmq9j6 Power flow
xzfspuv 1 · Batteries 1 and 2 (36 V each, 23 cells) → console breakers CB1–CB4 → buses A, B (battery 1) and C, D (battery 2). They are not connected in series.
qlm39gb 2 · The buses feed the DCE through CB5–CB10 (each load picks one of two buses).
gezpurs 3 · The T-handle sets the PWM duty cycle and the direction (relays).
8jzns5f 4 · The DCE switches 36 V to the 4 drive motors and the 2 steering motors.
nt1vmwm 5 · CB14 (AUX) takes buses A and C and powers the LCRU through the auxiliary connector.
l72bec1 Steering and suspension
t9eu8x6 TV camera: pan, tilt and filters
wvkh3dt Video to Earth
kugk4wi Opening and separation
pdvjwr1 Dust covers and lids: first the cover swings, then the lid is removed (virtual opening).
q01vx9g Module separation: each box moves away from its place; the cables follow it.
5trrvcx Exploded view on top of the opening and separation: the movements add up, they don't overlap.

# lrv3-modelo.js
b1mqlbq LRV at station 8 (EVA-3), side view (LPI Apollo Image Atlas: «STA 8; SPL 8135; LUNAR ROVING VEHICLE»)
fhs92k6 front 3/4 photo provided by the team
z32cq3a unverified identifier
5tbjli7 EVA-2 (Dec 12, 1972), vehicle stopped at a station
pivxg12 The RIGHT REAR fender extension replaced by 4 laminated maps joined with gray tape and 2 clamps from the optical alignment telescope (NASM).
x22rkzp Dust covers of the batteries, DCE and SPU closed (they were opened between EVAs to radiate heat; MSC-07464 §3.2).
s1s3o50 LCRU blanket open (panels hanging, mirrors exposed) and HGA pointed at Earth for TV (FM/TV mode, HSI-481184).
nr8pqek structure
zf3t71c An aluminum chassis in three sections with hinges and locking pins: it folded to travel in the lunar module's bay.
wu0tfek mobility
tn8hyq3 Four steel-mesh wheels with chevrons; each with a DC motor, an 80:1 harmonic drive and a brake. Independent front and rear Ackermann steering and a parallel-arm suspension with torsion bars.
jd6uwvu Crew station
apcoio2 Two folding seats of tube and webbing, a navigation and control console with 14 breakers, and the T-shaped hand controller.
oq2c36f Power and navigation
h8f2339 Two 36 V silver-zinc batteries (23 cells), four buses (A–D), a signal processing unit (SPU), a directional gyro (DGU) and drive control electronics (DCE).
5oixald communications
on3g3oa An LCRU with a 29 V internal battery, a hand-pointed 3 ft high-gain antenna, a low-gain antenna, a VHF antenna and a GCTA TV camera with an SIT tube controlled from Houston.
8mjw9by Cargo and science (Apollo 17)
n0xk2c6 Rear pallet and tool carrier, sample bag, traverse gravimeter (TGE) and the receiver of the SEP experiment with its three-loop antenna.
k025s4h Geometry could not be merged
gu7cf1c inferred
lb4vx5t documented
ifvv9xr An open wire-mesh tire; chevrons cover 50% of the contact; it tolerates ~10% broken wires.
44yvzts educational
0g1z2n2 Woven zinc-coated steel wires; they are drawn thicker and farther apart than the real ones so they can be seen on screen.
3rp3szg A 25.5 in inner frame (bump stop): it limits how much the outer frame deforms on impacts.
84xljze An aluminum disk that joins the mesh to the gearbox output; shape taken from the photo.
f445omg Ribbed floor panels of the center section.
5x056p8 Cross members and side rails under the panels; position and number inferred.
1hec5gf Hinges
8ld10ga Attachment points to the lunar module; position inferred.
vhafbup A pair of parallel wishbones between the chassis and the drive; each arm has its own torsion bar (upper ~15% of the load, lower ~85%).
cno9za5 A brushed series DC motor (36 V, PWM control), an 80:1 harmonic drive and a mechanical brake; sealed at 7.5 psia. The motor fittings form the king pin.
rz7pkhd A steering arm joined to the tie rod; geometry inferred (drawing not legible).
xwf9vqr A linear damper (silicone oil) between the chassis and the upper arm: 6 in of compression and 4 in of extension.
bzi0q71 Front
pfg68la Front
2ysx95s Rear
ry89q6c A split-field DC motor + gearbox + spur gear sector that moves the steering linkage. Front and rear are mechanically independent; the rear could be re-engaged with a tool.
fzigyy3 Sector and output arm to the tie rods; layout inferred (drawing 4.6 not legible).
zirsqnb Left
bi1a2nn Right
496rsgk front
wanc99t rear
q6n7ke4 A tie rod between the steering sector and the wheel arm.
absvihx NASM (fender extension of epoxy-impregnated fiberglass)
lhuuck6 Fiberglass fenders: they keep dust from covering the crew and the equipment.
g4w54h6 An improvised extension: 4 of the traverse maps joined with gray tape and held with 2 clamps from the LM's optical alignment telescope (the original broke at the end of EVA-1).
bxyd4na 2 clamps from the optical alignment telescope (shape inferred).
tn6rebj An adjustable webbing belt with a hook buckle; routing and buckle inferred.
ftm1rx1 Angled footrest.
2cwttzf Control and display console: navigation on top (attitude, IPI heading, bearing, range, distance) and monitoring/control below (speed, batteries, switches, 14 breakers).
p43jfi7 Panel layout: educational reconstruction.
pql19mb Gauge bezels, levers (PWM, drive enable, steering, ±15 V, NAV, AUX) and breaker buttons CB1–CB14.
yn5mwg6 The console's caution and warning flag.

eeabimv A primary silver-zinc battery, 23 cells in series, 36 V nominal, 121 Ah; relief valve 3.1–7 psid. It feeds buses A (CB1) and B (CB3).
vr896w2 A primary silver-zinc battery, 23 cells, 36 V, 121 Ah. It feeds buses C (CB2) and D (CB4); heat sink for the DGU.
plnaxij Signal processing unit: it combines heading and odometer pulses for bearing, range and distance. Eicosane wax (2.25 lb) and a thermal strap to battery 1.
o1sytoc Directional gyro unit: it outputs the heading as a 3-wire synchro; battery 2 is its heat sink.
gb5pe3e Drive control electronics: PWM 1 and PWM 2, direction relays, current-limited power transistors, odometer inhibit and the steering servo electronics. Octadecane wax (3.5 lb).
dmjvmjj lid
5j4z00y Housing lid (virtual inspection opening; in flight the housing was closed).
v7ignkf Housing pressure relief valve (opens at 3.1–7 psid).

0ac2dyf Mounts for the batteries and electronics.
zm8a6s6 An insulated dust cover; closed during the EVA (bimetallic actuators close it), opened between EVAs so the mirror can radiate heat.

d13trd2 A mast that fits into the left bumper fitting and locks with a bayonet collar.
eiem9se A manual pointing gimbal in azimuth and elevation.
h5t77ww A 3 ft parabolic reflector of mesh and ribs; nominal gain 24 dB, 20 W.
jq5csfc An optical sight with a reticle and a sector mask for pointing at Earth.
wkzvn98 «Mechanical pointing is done by tilting the handle in azimuth and elevation.»
752qjm1 Positioning mechanism (2.45 lb with the antenna); during an EVA the elevation was set by hand (e.g. 45°).
6c1ph69 A 5.13 in cup reflector.
kuswwf1 A helical feed, right-hand circular polarization, nominal gain 10 dB.
iko92dv A white cover that wraps the helix in the photos; the manual doesn't describe it.
uw9spks A tubular staff with a conical end in a keyed fitting on the frame; a swing-down hinge to remove the LCRU without taking off the GCTA.
x278z8f The TCU's lower electronics box (control unit): it receives the 70 kHz subcarrier and +29 V from the LCRU; it houses the azimuth axis.
30m9hy9 Azimuth thrust tube: a 487:1 gearmotor and 3.64:1 spur gears (gold liner according to photos).
66sqtcc TCU · Y-cable input
758cp00 Turntable and yoke: pan 134° to the left and 214° to the right, 3.03°/s.

h7h2xz8 The camera's mounting plate with the elevation spiroid gear segment (+85° / −45°, 3.12°/s).

4cykt43 A carrying handle and a small radiator (opened in the shade when not in use).
wqfnf4j A 9-digit display (on for 20 s), GRAV / READ / BIAS buttons and a power switch.
dxvnklx The receiver of the surface electrical properties experiment: optical reflectors to cool it under blankets that opened; it shut off above ~108 °F.

cq9ftu5 power
63q71uh Battery 1 feeds bus A through CB1 and bus B through CB3 (the breakers are on the console).
sijhu44 harness routing inferred
ac2ni79 Battery 2 → console harness (buses C and D)
ixv2icw Battery 2 feeds bus C through CB2 and bus D through CB4. The batteries are NOT in series (they don't make 72 V) or permanently in parallel: each load picks a bus.
ywt3yla routing inferred
3xh4ulv Console → DCE harness (buses A–D to drive and steering)
bdrh79l LF/RF from bus A or C (CB5, CB6), LR/RR from bus B or D (CB7, CB8); front steering A or C (CB9), rear B or D (CB10).
r2hmoxa a single bundle represents the circuits; routing inferred
hr4z3li DCE → front left drive motor (LF)
ftz8y44 PWM 1 or 2 modulates the 36 V to the motor (series DC, brushed); the odometer's 9 pulses per turn come back.
k7gdtsg DCE → front right drive motor (RF)
7fwk0cs PWM power to the RF motor and odometer pulses back.
nv82bhq DCE → rear left drive motor (LR)
h4s1b2b PWM power to the LR motor and odometer pulses.

l8dxdcq DCE → front steering motor
y0c9hx7 Steering servo with a feedback potentiometer; current limited to 1.8 A (bus A or C, CB9).
a2g1gee DCE → rear steering motor
xlapeav Same design as the front; bus B or D (CB10). Mechanically independent from the front.
n60nash T-shaped hand controller → DCE (throttle, steering, reverse)
m8sh5c8 The handle's deflection sets the PWM duty cycle; the DCE relays set the direction.
v8pjcyt DGU → SPU (heading, 3-wire synchro)
rg84mta The directional gyro outputs the heading as a three-wire synchro transmitter.
67f1ai6 SPU → console (heading, bearing, distance, speed)
5c22p5q The SPU combines odometer pulses (0.245 m/pulse) and heading; the console shows the IPI, bearing, range and distance.
xsaih0p Brake cable → front left wheel
5iwcg05 A mechanical brake worked by a cable from the controller (pulling back brakes; it locks at 12°).
4qxugoc Brake cable → front right wheel
6ww4cdu A mechanical brake worked by a cable from the controller.
iau0ehq Brake cable → rear left wheel
orsos0c Brake cable → rear right wheel
lv14567 SPU – battery 1 thermal strap (140 layers of foil)
thsjek4 Battery 1 acts as a partial heat sink for the SPU.
kt28zrk DGU – battery 2 thermal strap (2 layers of foil)
cmmedkz Battery 2 is the DGU's heat sink.
zfwulkd Console (CB14 AUX) → front auxiliary connector
b1i12up AUX takes power from both batteries through buses A and C (CB14) to the front connector.
0ik0w3d AUX connector → LCRU (external power)
sgztt2p With the selector on EXT, the LCRU uses 32–44 V from the rover and its DC-DC converter supplies 28.5 V and 16.5 V.
lltadc9 LCRU (HGA connector, red) → high-gain antenna
veqc5v2 S-band: color TV and voice/data to Earth with the vehicle stopped (FM/TV mode).
81j16hh routing along the mast inferred from photos
jo4onhr LCRU (LGA connector, blue) → low-gain antenna
k5wuxju LCRU → omnidirectional VHF antenna
qt1bvle LCRU (GCTA line) → TCU, «Y» cable
siwatul The LCRU supplies +29 V and the 70 kHz command subcarrier; the camera sends back composite video.
ykr2ow5 TCU → CTV camera (3.5 ft cable)
wfu0aya Video, power and control between the control unit (TCU) and the camera.
581f0xg 3-loop antenna → SEP receiver
92d2e63 Three orthogonal loops measure the three components of the magnetic field.
ywyb493 The data was recorded on magnetic tape; the DSEA was removable and came back to Earth.
y8kmzd8 SPU → SEP receiver (navigation data)
p9pi4gi The SEP recorded bearing increments (10°), distance (100 m) and the rover's odometer pulses.
dryec9q that the link comes from the SPU and its routing are inferred
o2l91e0 LCRU: 29 V internal battery → INT/EXT selector
m6kokut A 19-cell primary silver-zinc battery: 29 V (16.8 V tap), 400 Wh.
azevq2n LCRU: external input → DC-DC converter
3p6cvdx It accepts 32–44 V from the rover; it supplies 28.5 V and 16.5 V.
ib0ly8x LCRU: regulator → transceivers and processors
tx3m8xm A redundant low-voltage regulator powers the radio and signal modules.
6nabhbt educational layout
hj17m2p LCRU: downlink processor (DLSP) → S-band transceiver no. 2 (FM)
apknxcp It separates transmitting and receiving on the same antenna.
syb2idn GCTA: low-voltage supply → SIT high-voltage module
aqhqo0f The high-voltage module supplies 3 to 9 kV to the SIT tube.
wz95eqp GCTA: SIT tube → video preamplifier
5rza3yy A low-noise FET preamplifier, ALC/AGC, gamma ≈0.7 and aperture correction.
